I use Github regularly. It's literally one of the only ways (Github-alternatives included) to properly code a big project and maintain direct communications and surveillance overview of the team's code without making a mess of things. If you want to code separately, there are multiple branches to work in. Then you can merge when you feel like your code is synchronized with the methods/classes of the other code.

Github also has some pretty neat tools to sync codes throughout machines and MOST IMPORTANTLY, it can Ctrl+Z code from other branches as well as your own code on top of having a pretty wide integration with very popular IDEs such as Eclipse.

It's not REVOLUTIONARY it's just extremely extremely convenient (and more popular than BitBucket).

That's for closed projects.

For open projects, different devs can also contribute from the outside making it a really popular tool of open-source communities.
